rationale: The two are structurally identical: mutex-protected counters and an embedded readWriteCounter. B has nicer doc comments and the clearer field name `bytes`. However, B only adds to the byte count when err == nil. That goes against the io.Reader and io.Writer contracts, which allow a call to return n > 0 together with an error such as io.EOF or a short write. Those bytes were really transferred, so B under-counts in exactly the case a billing wrapper must get right. A always counts the returned n, which is the correct and idiomatic behaviour. B's documentation does not outweigh that robustness issue, so A is better.
